summary: The Expedited Disability Insurance Payments for Terminally Ill Individuals Act of 2026 establishes a phased-in payment structure for Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits during the waiting period for individuals diagnosed with a terminal illness. Terminally ill individuals must submit a diagnosis certified by at least two unrelated physicians who are not in the same practice group. The bill also mandates reports to Congress by the Social Security Administration and the Government Accountability Office regarding the provision and administration of these benefits.

affected_groups.effect: May receive phased-in Social Security Disability Insurance payments during the waiting period upon submitting a diagnosis certified by two eligible physicians.
Must administer the phased-in payments and coordinate with the Inspector General to submit annual evaluation reports to Congress.
Must submit a report evaluating the provision of these disability insurance benefits within two years of enactment.

key_provisions: Provides phased-in SSDI benefits for individuals determined to have a terminal illness.
Sets benefit amounts for the first two consecutive calendar months to 50 percent and 75 percent, respectively, of the standard calculated benefit.
Adjusts subsequent monthly benefit amounts over specific 12-month periods and sets benefits after 24 consecutive months at 95 percent of the standard amount.
Requires a terminal illness diagnosis to be certified by at least two unrelated physicians who are not in the same physician group practice.
Directs the Social Security Administration to submit annual reports to Congress evaluating the benefits, total expenditures, and recommendations to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse.
Directs the Government Accountability Office to submit a report within two years evaluating the benefit provision and providing recommendations for improvement.
Applies the amendments to benefits payable for months beginning after December 31, 2026.

summary_detail.significance: The bill alters the timing and structure of Social Security Disability Insurance payments for terminally ill applicants by introducing a phased-in payment schedule during the standard waiting period. Because the source material does not contain data on the exact number of individuals affected, total financial costs, or broader economic outcomes, the wider significance can only be understood through its specific administrative and payment adjustments for terminally ill claimants.
